The waveform at $t=1.5\mathrm{s}$ is as shown in the figure, and at this moment, the wave has just reached $x=3\mathrm{m}$.

1. What is the wave speed of this wave?
2. After how much additional time will the particle at $x=6\mathrm{m}$ appear at the trough position for the first time?

method.method_draft: Use a phase/delay analysis. First read the graph at t=1.5 s: the disturbed part extends from x=0 to the wavefront at x=3 m; the source point x=0 is at a trough y=-10 cm, and the crest is near x=2 m. From the text, the source began at t=0 and the front has just reached x=3 m at t=1.5 s, so v=3/1.5=2 m/s. Treat the motion at any position x as the source motion delayed by x/v. The graph shows the source is at its first trough at t=1.5 s. For x=6 m, the delay is 6/2=3 s, so the same first-trough phase occurs at absolute time 1.5+3=4.5 s. Since the question asks for additional time after t=1.5 s, the answer is 4.5-1.5=3 s.
